verifications.claim: 2 Chronicles 7:11–22 records God’s response to Solomon after the Temple dedication.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'After a dedicated time of prayer, the Lord appears to Solomon at night'; R3: 'Thus Solomon finished the house... Then the LORD appeared'; R4: v11 'Thus Solomon finished... v12 And the Lord appeared'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm the passage follows temple completion/dedication with God's appearance/response to Solomon.

verifications.claim: Solomon successfully completes the Temple and his palace before the divine appearance in 2 Chronicles 7:11–22.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Thus Solomon finished the house of the LORD and the king’s house... he successfully accomplished. Then the LORD appeared'; R4: v11 'Thus Solomon finished the house of the Lord, and the king's house... he prosperously effected. v12 And the Lord appeared'
verifications.reasoning: Direct sequence in v11 (completion) before v12 (appearance) explicitly stated in all Bible texts.

verifications.claim: The divine appearance in 2 Chronicles 7:11–22 happens at night.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the Lord appears to Solomon at night'; R3: 'Then the LORD appeared to Solomon in the night'; R4: v12 'the Lord appeared to Solomon by night'
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state the appearance is 'at night' or 'by night' in v12.

verifications.claim: 2 Chronicles 7:12-16 describes God choosing the Temple as a place for sacrifice and hearing prayer.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: v12 'chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice'; v15 'my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayer'; R4: v12 'chosen this place to myself for an house of sacrifice'; v15 'mine eyes shall be open, and mine ears attent unto the prayer'
verifications.reasoning: Verses 12,15-16 directly describe choosing for sacrifice and attentive to prayer.

verifications.claim: 2 Chronicles 7:12-16 records God promising: "if my people... humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land".
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4 v14: 'If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.'
verifications.reasoning: Exact or near-exact quote from v14 across all Bible versions and commentaries.

verifications.claim: 2 Chronicles 7:17-22 records God telling Solomon that if he and his descendants turn away, serve other gods, and break the covenant, Israel will be uprooted from the land.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: v19 'if you turn aside... serve other gods... v20 then I will pluck you up from my land'; R4: v19 'if ye turn away... serve other gods... v20 Then will I pluck them up by the roots out of my land'
verifications.reasoning: Verses 17-20 directly state conditional judgment of uprooting from the land for turning away, serving other gods.

verifications.claim: 2 Chronicles 7:17-22 records God telling Solomon that if he and his descendants turn away, serve other gods, and break the covenant, the Temple will be ruined.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: v20 'this house... I will cast out of my sight... v21 everyone passing by will be astonished'; R8 (NIV): 'This temple will become a heap of rubble'; R4: v20 'this house... will I cast out of my sight... v21 an astonishment'
verifications.reasoning: Verses 20-21 describe the temple as cast out, proverb/byword, astonishment/ruin for same conditions.
